title: Jar clocks Rs 208 Cr operating revenue in FY25, turns profitable in H2
passage: Jar's savings app reported operating revenue of Rs 208 crore during FY25 ending March 2025. The surge in scale came after the company vertically integrated its gold stack, which pushed its gross revenue to Rs 2,450 crore during the period. Vertical integration implies that Jar became a principal seller in FY25; it now owns the gold, manages the value chain, stores the asset, and records the full transaction value as revenue -- rather than only serving as a middleman routing user savings into gold through external partners. The Bengaluru-based startup reduced its net losses (excluding ESOP costs) to Rs 35.23 crore, and turned fully profitable in the last two consecutive quarters (January-March 2025 and April-June 2025). Jar has built a base of over 35 million registered users across 12,000 pin codes. The article provides no FY24 comparison figures.

title: Jar in talks to raise $100 Mn led by Westbridge
passage: Bengaluru-based fintech startup Jar is in advanced discussions to raise over $100 million in a new funding round led by Westbridge, at a term sheet valuing the company in the range of $500-550 million. Kotak Investment Banking has been appointed as the banker for the transaction; the deal is expected to close in the next 4 to 6 weeks from the article date. Jar's previous Series B (August 2022) raised $22.6 million led by Tiger Global at a $300+ million valuation, with other investors including Arkam Ventures, Tribe Capital and WEH Ventures. This new round, as of the article date, is NOT confirmed or closed.

title: Tiger Global leads $32M Series A in savings and investments app Jar
passage: Jar, a Bengaluru-based savings and investment startup, raised $32 million in Series A financing led by New York-headquartered Tiger Global, at a valuation of over $200 million according to two people familiar with the matter (co-founders declined to comment). Other investors include Rocketship.vc, Stonks, Force Ventures, Arkam Ventures, and individual investors including Klarna founder Victor Jacobsson. Jar was co-founded by Nishchay Ag (CEO) and Misbah Ashraf (Chief Product Officer), and had raised a $4.5 million seed round the previous year from Tribe Capital and Arkam Ventures. At the time of the Series A, Jar had over 4 million users, 99% investing in any asset class for the first time, and was seven months old.

title: Why digital gold savings startup Jar is under Karnataka police scanner
passage: Koramangala police station in Bengaluru registered an FIR against Jar Gold Retail Private Limited on January 16 under the Banning of Unregulated Deposit Schemes (BUDS) Act, 2019, alleging the company collected money from the public through a digital gold savings scheme without regulatory approval, and that it is not registered with SEBI or any other financial regulator. The FIR also alleges Jar offered referral bonuses of 30-40% to incentivise users to bring in new participants. Separately, an RBI market surveillance alert on July 20, 2025 raised concerns about the legality of the business model, and SEBI issued a public warning on November 8, 2025 stating that trading in digital or e-gold products is currently an unregulated activity. Jar's directors obtained anticipatory bail; the CID continues to investigate. Jar stated it operates only as a micro-savings and investment platform and that no customer has filed a complaint alleging non-delivery of gold or failure to return money.

title: About Jar - India's No. 1 Gold Savings App
passage: Jar is India's No. 1 Gold Savings App, trusted by 4+ Cr Indians saving daily, weekly or monthly in 24k gold starting from Rs 10. Gold purchased on Jar is secured with BRINKS, a globally recognised gold vaulting partner, and insured by ICICI Lombard.
